name: Solana: unvalidated account substituted for a program-owned PDA
requires: an Anchor program that reads state from an account it is supposed to own
the program id, and the genuine PDA the program derives for that role
a local validator, cloned from the cluster under test when the program is deployed
instruction data built from the IDL that names the account position under test
a funded payer keypair able to create a substitute account owned by the system program
questions: Does the Accounts struct mark the expected PDA with `Account<'info, T>`, which checks the owner and the discriminator, or with `UncheckedAccount` or `AccountInfo`?
If seeds are declared, does the seed list cover every field that distinguishes one user's account from another's, or only a constant prefix?
Can the caller pass an account whose owner is the system program or a token program where the handler assumes its own layout and deserializes the bytes anyway?
Does the handler re-derive the PDA with `find_program_address` and compare, or trust the address it was given?
Where does value leave the program on this path, and is the recipient taken from the account list or from a field the program itself wrote?
Is the account writable and owned by the caller at the moment of substitution, so a successful call changes bytes the attacker controls?
Does closing or reallocating the account happen before the ownership check, leaving a window where a foreign account is already trusted?
false_positives: `Account<'info, T>` already performs an owner check and a discriminator check, so a substitute of the wrong type is rejected before the handler
The PDA is re-derived with `find_program_address` and compared with `require_keys_eq!`, which is equivalent to a seeds constraint
The substituted account is accepted but the handler only reads a field the attacker cannot influence, so no value moves
The program is immutable and the account in question is a well-known program account that cannot be created by an attacker
The instruction is `#[access_control(...)]` gated, and the gate rejects the substitute before the body deserializes it
poc_must_show: the caller-owned substitute account's lamport balance before and after, read from the same validator, showing value the program meant for its own PDA
the owner of the substitute printed before and after, so a reader can tell a system-owned account that gained value from one that was rejected outright
a control run passing the genuine program-owned PDA, showing it does not pay the substitute, which is what attributes the gain to the substitution
impact_bar: Reportable when a substitute account the caller controls receives lamports or token balances that the program intended for its own PDA, quantified in lamports or token units. Informational when the substitute is accepted but nothing of value moves, or when Anchor's Account wrapper already rejects it and only the harness was wrong.
